biography.plain_text: Milton 'Milt' Sender is an American entrepreneur who co-founded Daymon Associates with Peter Schwartz in 1970. The business became Daymon Worldwide, a specialist in developing and marketing retailers' own-brand products. Sender led it as chief executive and chairman, helping shift private labels from low-price substitutes towards differentiated store brands as the company expanded internationally.

long_biography.plain_text:
Under Milton Sender's chairmanship, Daymon Worldwide developed software to find opportunities in store-level product sales. The firm also built private-label programmes for retailers across several countries, treating packaging, quality and marketing as parts of a store brand rather than as afterthoughts. Sender had co-founded the business with Peter Schwartz and continued to chair it after stepping down as chief executive.

He worked with suppliers and retailers on common product data, serving on the board of GS1, the standards organisation behind global product identifiers. At the Food Marketing Institute he helped establish a private-label initiative and promoted better traceability for goods. Following Schwartz's death, Sender and Daymon supported research into early cancer detection at Massachusetts General Hospital.
